from.place: The proof clause invoking Cohomology of Sheaves, Lemma 20.26.9 (Stacks Tag 06YD): the stalk of each flat sheaf module is a flat module.

title: Stalks of flat sheaves are flat modules
statement: Let (X,\mathcal O_X) be a ringed space and let \mathcal F be a flat \mathcal O_X-module sheaf [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], meaning that tensoring with \mathcal F preserves short exact sequences of \mathcal O_X-modules. For every point x of X, the stalk \mathcal F_x is a flat module over the stalk ring \mathcal O_{X,x}, meaning that tensoring with \mathcal F_x preserves exact sequences of \mathcal O_{X,x}-modules.

proof.text: Fix x and an acyclic three-term complex M^\bullet of \mathcal O_{X,x}-modules. The termwise skyscraper complex i_{x,*}M^\bullet is acyclic and its stalk at x is M^\bullet by [lem-pc-skyscraper-complex].

source.place: Modules, Lemma 17.17.2 (Tag 05NE), proof of (1) => (2), skyscraper complex

proof.text: Since \mathcal F is flat, the functor \mathcal G\mapsto\mathcal G\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal F is exact by [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Applying it to the acyclic complex i_{x,*}M^\bullet shows that i_{x,*}M^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal F is acyclic.

Stalk exactness [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact] makes the stalk at x of this tensor complex acyclic. Applying [lem-pc-ringed-space-module-stalk-tensor] degreewise identifies it with M^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}\mathcal F_x. Hence tensoring every exact three-term complex M^\bullet with \mathcal F_x on the right remains exact, which is precisely flatness of \mathcal F_x.

statement_change.what: For a general ringed space the stalk ring need not be local: on a one-point space with structure ring Z, its unique stalk is Z, which has multiple maximal ideals. Replace only the erroneous adjective local by stalk; no locally ringed hypothesis is added.
